udl2-tabular.def: Inputs that are vectors of fixed size whose entries always mean the same thing in the same order, like the columns of a spreadsheet.

udl2-model.def: An equation \(\by=\mathrm{f}[\bx,\bphi]\) of fixed form; it describes a family of input–output relations, and the parameters pick one member.

udl2-inference.def: Computing the output \(\by\) from an input \(\bx\) by running it through a (trained) model.

udl2-parameters.def: The adjustable numbers inside a model (Greek letters in Prince). Training chooses them.

udl2-training-set.def: The \(I\) example pairs \(\{\bx_i,\by_i\}\) used to choose the parameters.

udl2-loss.def: One number measuring the mismatch between model predictions and true outputs on the training set; smaller is better. Least squares: \(\sum_i(\mathrm{f}[x_i,\bphi]-y_i)^2\).

udl2-training.def: Finding \(\hat\bphi=\argmin_{\bphi}L[\bphi]\), the parameters with the smallest loss.

udl2-test-data.def: Examples not used for training, used to measure how well the model generalises.

udl2-residual.def: The gap between a prediction and the truth for one example, \(\mathrm{f}[x_i,\bphi]-y_i\).

udl2-gradient.def: The vector of partial derivatives of the loss with respect to each parameter; it points uphill on the loss surface.

udl2-gd.def: Repeatedly update \(\bphi\leftarrow\bphi-\alpha\,\partial L/\partial\bphi\): small steps downhill on the loss surface.

udl2-underfitting.def: The model is too simple to capture the true relation: training and test loss are both high.

udl2-overfitting.def: The model describes quirks of the training data that are not real: low training loss, high test loss.

udl2-objective.def: Any function that is maximised or minimised; loss and cost functions are objectives.

udl2-discriminative.def: A model \(y=\mathrm{f}[x,\bphi]\) that predicts the output directly from the measurement.

udl2-generative.def: A model \(x=\mathrm{g}[y,\bphi]\) of how the measurement is produced from the quantity of interest; prediction requires inverting it.
